Remove rows without f0 and mark the gaps they leave

Source: R/gaps.R
drop_rows_without_f0.Rd

Removes the rows whose f0 is missing, and adds a column, voiced_run, that numbers the stretches with f0 in each token: 1 up to the token's first gap, 2 after it, and so on. The time column still shows each gap as a longer step, and voiced_run keeps it whatever is done to the rows later. This is what the app's Start page does when "Remove rows without f0" is ticked. screen_f0_rows() gives the counts first.

Usage

drop_rows_without_f0(
  data,
  token = "token",
  time = "time",
  f0 = "f0",
  run = "voiced_run",
  gap_ratio = 1.5,
  min_run = 1,
  unvoiced = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format: one row per f0 sample.

token, time, f0

Column names. Defaults "token", "time", "f0". time must be the real time column. f0 is the one column that decides which rows have f0.

run

Name of the column to add. Default "voiced_run". When the column is there already, its gaps are kept (see Details). NULL adds no column and reads none.

gap_ratio

A time step longer than this many times the token's usual step is a gap. Default 1.5. Must be above 1. Inf reads gaps from rows without f0 only.

min_run

Samples a run at the start or end of a token must have to be kept. Default 1 keeps all samples with f0. 3 also removes runs of 1 or 2 samples cut off by a gap (see Details).

unvoiced

Values in the f0 column to read as no f0, such as -1 or c(0, -1), for a column in Hz whose tracker marks unvoiced frames this way. Default NULL: only NA counts as no f0.

Value

data without the rows without f0, of the same class (a data frame or a tibble), with the rows in their original order and all columns kept. The run column, an integer, is added as described in Details. Attribute rows_without_f0 is a list:

  • f0 and unvoiced: the column screened and the values read as no f0.

  • rows: rows in data.

  • removed: rows removed in all.

  • start, end, inside: rows without f0 removed at the start, at the end, and inside tokens. no_f0: rows removed with the tokens with no f0. no_time: rows without f0 that cannot be placed, as they or the token's samples with f0 have no time.

  • short_runs: samples with f0 removed by min_run.

  • tokens_lost: the tokens removed entirely, as text.

  • gaps_rows: gaps in the output from rows that were removed.

  • gaps_time_only: gaps in the output found only from the time steps, as in the summary of screen_f0_rows().

  • gaps_run: gaps in the output that only the existing run column marked.

  • grid: the time-step details, as in screen_f0_rows().

Details

Which rows go. Run zero_hz_to_na() first, so that 0 Hz counts as no f0 in Hz columns. Then the values in unvoiced are read as NA in the f0 column, and every row whose f0 is NA (or NaN or infinite) is removed. Only the f0 column decides. 0 and negative values count as no f0 only through unvoiced, because in a signed or normalised column they are real values. A token with no f0 at all is removed entirely. A row with f0 but no time (NA) is kept, with voiced_run NA. On a regular grid its neighbours are then two steps apart, which reads as a gap, so with min_run = 3 a short run next to it at the token's start or end can go. A row whose token is NA belongs to a token of its own.

Short edge runs. With min_run = 3, runs of 1 or 2 samples that a gap cuts off at the start or end of a token go too: the samples before the token's first run of at least min_run samples, and after its last one. Runs are split at every gap, as in the run column below. A token with no run that long keeps all its samples. The default min_run = 1 removes no samples with f0. These samples have f0, so removing them moves the token's first or last f0, and with it the 0-1 time axes (token_t01, <tier>_t01 and the models' per-token rescale). Removing rows without f0 alone never moves those axes. Only runs at the token's start and end go: a short run next to a gap inside the token stays.

The run column. A gap is one of these:

  • one or more rows without f0 between two kept samples;

  • when the time steps form a regular grid, a step more than gap_ratio times the token's usual step, in a token that is not set aside (see screen_f0_rows());

  • a change in the value of an existing run column, such as the voiced_run of an earlier removal.

So data whose rows without f0 were removed beforehand get the same voiced_run as data with them kept, as long as the grid is regular and the token's usual step is one frame. And running this again on its own output, after more rows have lost their f0, keeps the gaps the first run marked, on any grid.

The column is added when rows are removed, or when the gaps make some token's runs go above 1. When neither happens, data is returned as it is, and a voiced_run column already there is left alone. Otherwise a column of that name is replaced, with a message, by one that still marks its gaps. On a grid that is not regular, the time steps cannot show the gaps, so run this on data that still has its rows without f0 or its voiced_run column.

contour_duration(), trim_to_voiced() and flag_f0_gaps() read the voiced_run column, so they give the same results on the output as on the data with the rows kept. Other columns, including has_gap and n_missing, are kept as they are.

See also

screen_f0_rows() for the counts before removal; zero_hz_to_na() to run first; contour_duration(), trim_to_voiced() and flag_f0_gaps(), which read voiced_run.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  token = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
  time  = rep(0.005 + 0.01 * (0:9), 2),
  f0    = c(NA, 200, 202, NA, NA, 206, 208, 209, NA, NA,
            NA, NA, 181, 183, 185, 187, 188, NA, 190, NA))
out <- drop_rows_without_f0(df)
out
#>    token  time  f0 voiced_run
#> 1      a 0.015 200          1
#> 2      a 0.025 202          1
#> 3      a 0.055 206          2
#> 4      a 0.065 208          2
#> 5      a 0.075 209          2
#> 6      b 0.025 181          1
#> 7      b 0.035 183          1
#> 8      b 0.045 185          1
#> 9      b 0.055 187          1
#> 10     b 0.065 188          1
#> 11     b 0.085 190          2
attr(out, "rows_without_f0")[c("removed", "start", "end", "inside")]
#> $removed
#> [1] 9
#> 
#> $start
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $end
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $inside
#> [1] 3
#> 

# The same voiced_run when the rows were removed beforehand: the time
# steps show the gaps
clean <- df[!is.na(df$f0), ]
identical(drop_rows_without_f0(clean)$voiced_run, out$voiced_run)
#> [1] TRUE

# Also remove the runs of 1 or 2 samples cut off at the start or end
drop_rows_without_f0(df, min_run = 3)
#>   token  time  f0 voiced_run
#> 1     a 0.055 206          1
#> 2     a 0.065 208          1
#> 3     a 0.075 209          1
#> 4     b 0.025 181          1
#> 5     b 0.035 183          1
#> 6     b 0.045 185          1
#> 7     b 0.055 187          1
#> 8     b 0.065 188          1

# A tracker that writes -1 for unvoiced frames
df2 <- data.frame(token = "c", time = 0.005 + 0.01 * (0:5),
                  f0 = c(-1, 150, 152, -1, 155, -1))
drop_rows_without_f0(df2, unvoiced = -1)
#>   token  time  f0 voiced_run
#> 1     c 0.015 150          1
#> 2     c 0.025 152          1
#> 3     c 0.045 155          2
